findings.detail: THE GATE CONTRADICTS ITSELF, AND THE F7 REPAIR IS WHAT DRIVES IT TWELVE TIMES A RUN. The repair's whole argument is that fabric/api.py::build refuses at `v < 0.0` and -0.0 is not less than 0.0, so FAB_<LEVER>=-0.0 assembles and the `<= 0.0` branches are entered with a negative zero. I confirmed the premise: on the arm {FAB_SOCIETY:1, nine levers at '-0.0'} the frozen Config holds -0.0 on all nine fields (math.copysign(1.0, v) == -1.0 on every one) and all nine reasons print '-0.0'. What nobody read is WHAT ONE OF THEM SAYS. fab.balance emits, in full: "FAB_BALANCE=-0.0: no load-balance pressure. This is 'off', not C2 -- the C2 alarm is fab.balance_nonzero reading 0 while this is above zero. The value is PRINTED rather than asserted to be 0, and a negative one cannot reach here at all: fabric/api.py::build refuses it at startup, because at balance_w<0 this term was still APPLIED, with its sign reversed, under this same reason." A minus sign in the equation and 'a negative one cannot reach here at all' in the next clause of the same sentence. I swept all 12 F7 arms and dumped every reason: this is the ONLY one of the class -- no other gate reason in fabric/api.py makes a reachability claim about negatives. THE STRICT DEFENCE AND WHY IT DOES NOT SAVE IT: in IEEE-754 -0.0 is a signed zero and `-0.0 < 0.0` is False, so build's refusal is not violated and the sentence is arguably true of 'negative' in the narrow sense. But the sentence is a DID IT FIRE report about the arm it is printing on, and on that arm the value it prints reads as negative to every reader who checks the arithmetic -- which is the exact standard the spine sets for an unreachable arm and the exact standard the nine reasons were repaired to meet. The text is pre-existing and unchanged since HEAD; what is new is that tests/test_fabric.py now enters this configuration on every run and its own report calls that arm the thing that makes the check work. AND THE REPAIR BLOCKS THE OBVIOUS FIX: I hardened build's refusal on a mirror to cover a signed zero (`v < 0.0 or (v == 0.0 and copysign(1.0, v) < 0.0)`); HEAD's tests/test_fabric.py stays green (exit 0, 8 checks 0 failing) and the CURRENT one DIES -- LeverError raised out of cfg() inside check_f7, uncaught, no '=== N checks ===' line printed at all, exit 1. So refusing -0.0 is now a suite crash rather than a reported finding, and the only repair compatible with the check is to reword the sentence. That is a real cost the repair did not name.
